overview: Yankuang Energy (formerly Yanzhou Coal Mining) is a Shandong, China-headquartered, dual-listed (HKEX H-share 1171.HK / SSE A-share 600188.SS) integrated coal and coal-chemicals group, and the largest listed thermal coal producer in China. It mines, washes and sells thermal, PCI and coking coal across Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Gansu, Inner Mongolia and Xinjiang in China and, through its 62%-owned Australian subsidiary Yancoal Australia, is the largest pure-play coal producer in Australia. The Group has diversified into coal chemicals (methanol, acetic acid, caprolactam and other derivatives), electricity generation, high-end mining equipment manufacturing, and intelligent (bulk commodity) logistics, and is majority-controlled (52.84%) by Chinese state-owned enterprise Shandong Energy Group Co., Ltd.

business_model.summary: Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional/commodity-price driven rather than recurring: the Group mines and sells coal (thermal, PCI and coking grades) directly to power, metallurgy, chemical and trading customers in China and export markets (Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Australia), and separately produces and sells coal-derived chemicals (methanol, acetic acid, caprolactam, ethylene glycol, urea, etc.). A smaller electricity-generation business and a growing bulk-logistics (rail/port/road) segment round out the mix. FY2025 segment sales: Coal RMB88.67bn (66.5% of RMB133.3bn total), Coal Chemicals RMB24.29bn (18.2%), Logistics RMB15.08bn (11.3%), Electricity RMB2.31bn (1.7%), Other RMB2.99bn (2.2%). Profitability is highly cyclical and tied to spot/contract coal and chemical product prices, which fell sharply from the FY2022 peak (coal sales price ~RMB650-950/ton across entities) through FY2025 before recovering into H1 2026.

revenue_streams.name: Coal chemicals (methanol, acetic acid, caprolactam, etc.)
revenue_streams.trend: growing volumes, margins improving on coal-to-chemicals cost advantage vs oil/gas

revenue_streams.name: Logistics (rail, port, road, bulk freight)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, +361% YoY sales income in FY2025 from new consolidations

revenue_streams.name: Electricity generation
revenue_streams.trend: being materially expanded via FY2026 power-asset acquisition from parent

business_model.customer_type: B2B — power generators, steel/metallurgical producers, chemical manufacturers, commodity traders; ~9.6% of FY2025 sales to a single largest (connected-party) customer, 15.7% to top five customers
business_model.geographic_mix: Domestic China sales ~77% of FY2025 coal sales income (RMB69.2bn of RMB88.7bn); overseas coal sales ~23% (Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Australia); overseas assets (mainly Yancoal Australia) were 17.3% of total Group assets at FY2025 year-end

main_competitors: Shandong Energy Group (parent, overlapping coal assets)
competitive_position.market_position: Leading thermal coal enterprise in China by the company's own characterization, and Yancoal Australia (62.26%-owned) is the largest pure coal producer in Australia; one of the largest listed coal-chemical producers in China with leading acetic acid production capacity.

moat_factors.description: 52.9bn tons in-situ domestic coal resources (China National Standard) plus 8.08bn tons overseas (JORC), among the largest reserve bases of any listed Chinese coal company, spanning Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Gansu, Inner Mongolia, Xinjiang and Australia

Coal-to-chemicals and now coal-to-power integration lowers input-cost volatility and captures margin across the value chain; six listed platforms (A-share, H-share, Yancoal Australia, SMT Scharf AG, etc.) support capital-raising flexibility

As a major SOE-controlled energy group, Yankuang benefits from implicit government support, access to low-cost financing (average financing rate down to 2.46% in FY2025), and alignment with national energy-security policy, but is also subject to state-directed pricing
National Enterprise Technology Center, 8.2-meter mining-height equipment, first domestic million-ton coal indirect-liquefaction demonstration facility; RMB3.4bn R&D spend (2.3% of revenue) in FY2025

Controlling shareholder Shandong Energy has committed to resolving 'horizontal competition' by progressively injecting its own coal and power assets into the listed vehicle (Xibei Mining 2025, Luxi Mining/Xinjiang Neng Hua 2023, new energy/power assets 2026), giving Yankuang a visible, though related-party-dependent, growth pipeline

weaknesses: Commodity price-taker with limited pricing power; profitability swings sharply with coal and chemical benchmark prices (net profit fell from RMB37.9bn in FY2022 to RMB8.5bn in FY2025)

Heavy reliance on, and transactions with, controlling shareholder Shandong Energy (largest supplier at 17.2% of FY2025 procurement; ~9.6% of sales to connected parties), creating related-party-transaction and minority-shareholder-interest governance risk
Complex multi-entity consolidated structure (12+ operating coal subsidiaries, varying ownership stakes from 42.64% to 100%) complicates minority-interest attribution and comparability

Revenue and per-share metrics suffer comparability breaks: FY2024 revenue was restated from RMB124.5bn to RMB141.1bn in the FY2025 annual report due to retrospective consolidation of businesses acquired under common control (Xibei Mining), and bonus share issues in 2023 and 2024 break historical per-share trends
High leverage: debt-to-equity ratio of 184.2% (total borrowings/shareholders' equity) at FY2025 year-end; net current liabilities position

growth_drivers: Continued asset injections from controlling shareholder Shandong Energy under its 'horizontal competition resolution' pledge — most recently the ~RMB16.4bn acquisition (announced June 2026) of Shandong Energy's New Energy Group (100%) and Shanneng Power Sales (100%) subsidiaries, adding ~13,252 MW of generation capacity and ~22.9bn kWh of annual output, aimed at coal-power integration to hedge coal-price cyclicality

Yancoal Australia's pending ~USD1.85bn upfront (plus up to USD550m contingent) acquisition of Kestrel Coal Group (80% JV interest in the Kestrel coking coal mine, Queensland), adding premium metallurgical coal to the product mix and diversifying the overseas portfolio

Major mine capacity build-out under the 15th Five-Year Plan: ~70 million tons of additional salable coal capacity targeted by project completions (Youfanghao, Huolinhe No.1, Liusangedan, Yangjiaping, Mafuchuan, Maojiachuan, Galutu mines) between 2027-2031, aiming for raw coal output >300 million tons

Expansion of high-end/new-material coal chemicals (olefins, coal-to-liquids, polyoxymethylene) with a target of raising high-end chemical products to >70% of the chemicals mix by the end of the 15th Five-Year Plan, benefiting from coal's cost advantage versus oil/gas-based routes amid elevated international energy prices

Diversification into non-coal minerals (Caosiyao molybdenum mine, ~1.04bn ton resource, targeted completion by 2028; Canadian potash mining rights, 1.7bn tons proven KCl reserves) to reduce single-commodity dependence
Planned spin-off/listing of Wubo Technology (smart logistics) to unlock value in emerging business segments
New energy build-out (wind, solar, storage, 'coal-power-storage-hydrogen' integration) targeting >10 million kW of new-energy generation capacity

business.description: Net profit fell ~78% from the FY2022 peak (RMB37.9bn) to FY2025 (RMB8.5bn) as coal sales prices dropped roughly 20% YoY in FY2025; earnings are highly sensitive to spot and contract coal prices which are themselves sensitive to Chinese macro demand, hydro/renewables output, and import policy

Company explicitly flags coal mining and coal chemicals as 'highly hazardous' with 'complex uncertainties' in production safety; any major mine safety incident could trigger production suspensions, regulatory penalties and reputational damage

Shandong Energy is both the largest supplier (17.2% of FY2025 procurement) and a top-five connected customer (9.6% of sales); asset injections from the parent (Xibei Mining, new power assets) raise questions about pricing fairness and minority-shareholder protection

FY2024 revenue was restated from RMB124.5bn to RMB141.1bn following retrospective consolidation of Xibei Mining as a business combination under common control; bonus share issues in 2023 and 2024 break per-share historical comparability

financial.description: Debt-to-equity ratio of 184.2% (total borrowings/shareholders' equity attributable to the Company) at FY2025 year-end; total borrowings of RMB131.3bn against RMB71.3bn of attributable equity; net current liabilities position (-RMB22.9bn)

Overseas coal sales priced in USD/AUD, foreign-currency deposits/borrowings, and imported equipment costs create FX translation risk; the Group booked a RMB227 million exchange loss in FY2025 despite partial hedging via forward contracts at Yancoal Australia/International

The ~RMB16.4bn parent power-asset acquisition and Yancoal's ~USD1.85-2.4bn Kestrel coal mine acquisition both require substantial cash/debt funding at a time of already-elevated leverage and cyclically depressed coal cash flows

regulatory.description: China's 'carbon peaking and carbon neutrality' commitments and tightening environmental regulation directly threaten the long-term growth and social license of the core coal business; management explicitly identifies this as a top risk in the annual report

regulatory.risk: State-directed coal pricing and supply policy
regulatory.description: Chinese coal prices are influenced by government supply-side policy (capacity verification/curtailment, import quotas, 'reasonable price band' guidance), which can compress or support margins independent of underlying supply-demand fundamentals

CSRC rules on market value management, related-party disclosure and corporate governance (including the 2025 abolition of the Supervisory Committee) continue to evolve, raising compliance costs and disclosure obligations for connected transactions with Shandong Energy

macro.description: Coal demand is tied to Chinese industrial production, power demand and construction activity; a broader economic slowdown would directly reduce coal and chemical volumes and prices

Coal's share of China's electricity generation has fallen below 50% as renewables penetration rises (~41% in some 2026 readings), posing a structural long-term headwind to thermal coal demand even as near-term supply tightness supports prices

Operations in Australia, Canada and Germany expose the Group to host-country policy, trade and foreign-investment-review risk (e.g., Australian regulatory approval needed for the Kestrel coal mine acquisition)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Mixed near-term picture: Chinese domestic coal supply-demand is expected to move from 'moderately loose' toward 'relatively balanced with periodic tightness' in 2026 per management, with international coal and coal-chemical prices supported by elevated oil/gas prices from geopolitical tensions (Middle East). Longer-term, Chinese coal demand growth is expected to plateau and decelerate as the energy transition and renewables penetration accelerate, though an abrupt decline is viewed as unlikely over the current five-year planning horizon (15th Five-Year Plan, 2026-2030).
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — a classic commodity cyclical; net profit fell roughly 78% peak-to-trough (FY2022 to FY2025) and then rebounded >50% YoY in H1 2026 as prices recovered
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — high absolute debt load (RMB131bn) means financing costs matter, though average financing rate fell to 2.46% in FY2025 reflecting benign domestic rates and state-linked credit access
key_input_costs: Labor/employee wages and welfare (~24.5% of self-produced coal cost)
Methanol/chemical feedstock and fuel costs (~74% of chemical product cost)
Land subsidence and environmental remediation costs

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 revenue rose 15.4% YoY to RMB70.2bn and net profit attributable to shareholders rose 57.2% YoY to RMB7.87bn, driven by rising coal and coal-chemical product prices and improved operations, reversing the FY2023-2025 earnings decline
Company issued a positive profit alert ahead of H1 2026 results, forecasting ~RMB7.2bn attributable profit, up ~53% YoY

Announced ~RMB16.4bn (RMB15.57bn + RMB0.85bn) cash acquisition of Shandong Energy's New Energy Group (100%) and Shanneng Power Sales (100%), adding ~13,252 MW of power generation capacity and ~22.9bn kWh of annual generation, explicitly framed as coal-power integration to hedge coal-price cyclicality and resolve horizontal competition with the parent; stock rose ~9% on the announcement

Yancoal Australia (62.26%-owned) agreed a binding deal to acquire 100% of Kestrel Coal Group (holding an 80% JV interest in the Kestrel coking coal mine, Queensland) for ~USD1.85bn upfront plus up to USD550m in contingent payments tied to coking coal prices, adding premium metallurgical coal to the portfolio

FY2025 results: sales income RMB133.3bn (-5.5% YoY), net profit attributable to shareholders RMB8.52bn (IFRS) / RMB8.38bn (CAS) (down from RMB14.6bn in FY2024-restated), amid declining coal and chemical prices; record salable coal production of 182.4 million tons aided by the Xibei Mining consolidation; debt-to-asset ratio reduced to 62.2%; final dividend of RMB0.32/share proposed (full-year RMB0.50/share)

Consolidated Xibei Mining (51%-owned, acquired for RMB14.07bn) as a business combination under common control with Shandong Energy, triggering retrospective restatement of FY2024 financials (revenue restated from RMB124.5bn to RMB141.1bn) and prior-period comparatives
Disposed of Xintai Coal (Xintai Meiye) subsidiary via public listing/auction (base price RMB670m, highest bid RMB3.05bn) as part of ongoing portfolio optimization/divestment of non-core assets

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Li Wei struck a cautiously optimistic tone for 2026, citing expectations that domestic coal supply-demand will tighten modestly and that geopolitically-driven oil/gas price strength will support coal-to-chemicals cost competitiveness and coal-chemical product pricing both domestically and internationally. Management emphasized a three-part 15th Five-Year Plan strategy: 'deeply cultivating core industries' (mining and chemicals capacity growth), 'fostering emerging industries' (equipment manufacturing, logistics, new energy as a 'second growth curve'), and 'deepening capital operations' (asset optimization, further coal/power asset injections from Shandong Energy, and continued resolution of horizontal competition with the controlling shareholder).

bull_case: H1 2026 results show a sharp cyclical recovery (+57% net profit YoY) as coal and coal-chemical prices rebound from the FY2025 trough, suggesting the worst of the down-cycle may be behind the stock

Visible, state-sponsored growth pipeline via parent Shandong Energy's commitment to resolve 'horizontal competition' through continued asset injections (Xibei Mining 2025, power assets 2026), giving line of sight to further scale and diversification largely outside the open market

Diversification into coal-power integration (2026 power-asset acquisition), premium coking coal (Kestrel acquisition via Yancoal Australia) and non-coal minerals (molybdenum, potash) reduces single-commodity thermal-coal dependence over time
Low and falling average cost of debt (2.46% in FY2025) and a large, diversified, multi-platform corporate structure provide financing flexibility despite a highly leveraged balance sheet
Coal-to-chemicals cost advantage versus oil/gas-based routes is structurally reinforced when international oil and gas prices are elevated (as in 2026), supporting the higher-margin chemicals segment
bear_case: Deeply cyclical, commodity price-taker earnings profile: net profit fell ~78% from the FY2022 peak to the FY2025 trough, and any renewed coal-price weakness (e.g., from a China growth slowdown or import surge) would quickly compress profitability again

Secular decarbonization and renewables-substitution policy in China (carbon peaking/neutrality commitments, falling coal share of power generation) creates a structural long-term headwind to the core coal business that management itself flags as a top risk

Heavy and recurring related-party dealing with controlling shareholder Shandong Energy (largest supplier and a top connected customer, plus asset-injection acquisitions) raises governance and fair-value concerns for minority H-share investors

High leverage (184% debt-to-equity) combined with large pending cash commitments (RMB16.4bn power-asset deal, up to ~USD2.4bn Kestrel coal mine deal) could pressure the balance sheet if coal prices soften before these investments generate offsetting cash flow

Reduced dividend payout target (cut to ~50% from ~60%) for 2026-2028 signals management's own more cautious capital-return stance, and repeated restatements/bonus issues (FY2024 revenue restated +13%, 2023/2024 bonus shares) complicate historical comparability for investors
